_purpose: Canonical P2-B read-only canary trust configuration. Admits exactly ONE decision: the founder-runtime organism-status read-only observation at authority class A0. No approvers exist, so no approval-gated (A2+) decision can ever verify; the only admitted operation is read_only; live mutation stays sealed. implementation_sha is a placeholder the launcher stamps with the verified git HEAD at start (scripts/p2b-decision-runtime.sh).
_identity_contract: expected_source_shas pins the git source SHA the requesting component honestly attests. source_lineage is the qualification history behind that pin: when the Founder Runtime advances, the new SHA is qualified here and the old one marked superseded — the pin is then REQUIRED to move (a config still pinning a superseded SHA is refused at validation as STALE_SOURCE_PIN, and a request presenting a superseded SHA is denied SOURCE_SHA_SUPERSEDED with the superseding SHA named). Identity is never falsified and never silently stale.

founder_runtime.qualification_note: T39: the Founder Runtime that exposes the mission AUTHORITY gate over HTTP. Until this SHA the external channel could only be driven in-process, so a founder's ALLOW arriving through the API produced a plan decision the mission kernel refuses. Its predecessor 20a184f36088be934ded5f8a93039d7aeabad86f is superseded by this very change — qualifying a runtime is what advancing it costs.

_lineage_note: superseded_by names the CURRENTLY QUALIFIED identity, not the immediate successor: validateTrustConfig requires every superseded entry to point at a qualified lineage SHA. superseded_at preserves the real retirement order. This lineage is kept identical to config/governance-v2-adoption-trust.json on purpose — the Founder Runtime's identity is one fact, and a SHA that is current on one surface must not read as stale on the other.
